item.title: Westwin town hall set for Monday
item.description: Westwin Elements is set to host a town hall on Monday, Feb. 2 at the Richmond Hill City Center in a bid to allay fears held by Bryan County residents regarding the company’s plans to establish a nickel refinery in Richmond Hill.

item.title: The story of the Salt Pillar, part 2
item.description: We have finally reached the sad conclusion to the story of the man called Lot. He was the nephew of one of the greatest men to ever live on earth, the Patriarch Abraham.

item.title: God’s consistency
item.description: This winter has seen so many extreme temperature swings; one week it is really warm and the next week really cold. The truth be told, weather in most places in the world is really inconsistent.

item.title: Spiritual growth is needed
item.description: The Apostle Peter wrote, “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby (I Peter 2:2). The people to whom Peter was writing had been and were suffering from persecution. They needed strength, both from the word of God and from other Christians. Peter serves as a perfect example of a Christian who knew how to encourage and uplift others.

item.title: Americana Corner: The early life of James Madison
item.description: James Madison was one of our nation’s most important Founding Fathers and played a critical role in shaping the United States. Known to history as the Father of the Constitution, Madison was not a dynamic leader of men but was perhaps the most useful subordinate of our Founding Fathers.

item.title: Wholesale Observations: Fort Pulaski National Monument
item.description: One of the major local tourist sites in Savannah is our very own Fort Pulaski, roughly halfway between Savannah and Tybee Island. It is a huge brickwork fort, built on a small island on the Savannah River. It was designed to protect the City of Savannah from enemy warships traveling up the Savannah River, whether British, Spanish, or any others.

item.title: Nutritional Wealth: Health swaps
item.description: Picture this: You’re over 50, staring down a doctor’s note with “cancer,” “heart disease,” or “diabetes” scribbled on it. The news hits like a rogue wave off the Georgia coast. But here’s what most people miss: One habit swap can buy you years. Two or three? That’s when the magic compounds—potentially adding a decade or more of quality life.

item.title: Editor’s Corner: In sickness and in health
item.description: In honor of the rampant, relentless flu season that is already adding to Coastal Georgia’s misery alongside potential snowfall set to arrive this weekend (seriously, Weather Channel, what on Earth is going on???) here are some poems that deal with the subject of illness, sickness, or recovery. Stay warm, folks, and do stock up on Vicks VapoRub and chicken broth; and also: try to find a choice novel and/or television series to keep you entertained as well. (Heated Rivalry, anyone?)

item.title: Letter to the editor: Suggestions to ease Hyundai-area traffic
item.description: I submitted the following info several months ago when GDOT sent out an email requesting comments on Hyundai-related traffic problems. Never heard back from them or saw anything in the media, so I assumed it was either lost or ignored. Neither idea is new or untried. It certainly isn’t bottle-rocker science.

item.title: Georgia DOT preps for another winter weather event: What to know
item.description: ATLANTA – The Georgia Department of Transportation (Georgia DOT) is preparing for another winter weather event expected to have impacts across much of the state, beginning during the early morning hours of Saturday, January 31.
